text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Israeli soldier killed in Hizbollah attack.
- U.S. envoy Dennis Ross begins Jerusalem-Ramallah shuttle.
- Maccabiah bridge collapse claims fourth victim.
- Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman threatens to quit if budget cut not endorsed. Treasury: 1997 inflation target won't be met.
- Government mulls charging cars to enter cities.
- 1997 investment aid down 15 percent.
- Croatia seeking Israeli defence, energy deals.
GLOBES
- Neeman: "I'll not remain as finance minister without the support of the coalition for my policy".
- Israel Aircraft Industries in negotiations to build planes for Federal Express for $1-2 billion.
HAARETZ
- Ross demands Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat immediately implement security measures.
- Neeman: Inflation target of Bank of Israel could raise unemployment.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Israeli soldier killed in Lebanon action.
- Koor to sell its part in Nesher.
- Copter camera spots speeders.
MAARIV
- Foreign currency reforms: Israelis will be able to buy apartments abroad.
- Government assessments: Bank of Israel will raise the interest rate by half a percentage point following rise in inflation expectations.
